name: COL4A1 or COL4A2-related cerebral small vessel disease with hemorrhagic tendency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed diagnostic criteria for COL4A1/COL4A2-related cerebral small vessel disease

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in COL4A1 or COL4A2 gene
MRI evidence of cerebral small vessel disease including white matter hyperintensities, lacunar infarcts, microbleeds, or intracerebral hemorrhages
History of spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage or hemorrhagic stroke
Family history of cerebral small vessel disease or intracerebral hemorrhage consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Presence of systemic features such as ocular anomalies or renal involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant plus characteristic neuroimaging findings and clinical evidence of hemorrhagic stroke or intracerebral hemorrhage
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of genetic, clinical, and imaging data; family history supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically lobar hemorrhages in young to middle-aged adults
Congenital or acquired cystic cavities in cerebral hemispheres

common.notes: Small deep infarcts due to small vessel occlusion
Diffuse or patchy periventricular and deep white matter changes
searchTerms: white matter spots on brain MRI
areas of increased signal in brain white matter

common.notes: Includes cataracts, microcornea, or other anterior segment anomalies

occasional.notes: May occur secondary to cortical involvement or hemorrhagic lesions
Resulting from ischemic or hemorrhagic strokes
searchTerms: weakness on one side of body
kidney cysts or blood in urine
kidney abnormalities with blood in urine

occasional.notes: More common in congenital or severe cases

rare.notes: Rare vascular malformations associated with COL4A1 mutations

rare.symptomName: Subclinical microbleeds detected on susceptibility-weighted imaging
searchTerms: microbleeds detected only on special MRI

laboratory: Genetic testing confirming pathogenic COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants
imaging: MRI brain showing white matter hyperintensities, lacunar infarcts, microbleeds, porencephalic cysts, and intracerebral hemorrhages
genetic: Autosomal dominant mutations in COL4A1 or COL4A2 genes
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Ophthalmologic examination revealing anterior segment dysgenesis

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement including angiokeratomas and renal failure

redFlags: Early-onset recurrent intracerebral hemorrhages without hypertension
Family history of stroke or hemorrhagic events in young adults
Presence of porencephalic cysts or congenital brain malformations
references: Meuwissen ME, Halley DJ, Smit LS, et al. The expanding phenotype of COL4A1 and COL4A2 mutations: clinical data on 13 newly identified families and a review of the literature. Genet Med. 2015;17(11):843-853.
Vahedi K, Bousser MG. Cerebral small vessel disease: genetic and clinical aspects. J Neurol Sci. 2019;405:116429.
Gould DB, Phalan FC, Breedveld GJ, et al. Role of COL4A1 in small-vessel disease and hemorrhagic stroke. N Engl J Med. 2006;354(14):1489-1496.
